text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Despite the social economic policy statement of Prime Minister Hariri's government , opposition groups called for a general strike and demonstration on Nov 28 in protest at what they called "violations of freedom and democracy" by the government.
-Military prosecuter charges a policeman for dealing with the Israeli Mossad.
-Arab bankers and financiers start a two-day conference in Beirut.
-MPs will start debating on Monday the government policy statement introduced by Prime Minister Hariri.
-Trans Mediterranian Airlines resume flights today after completing its administrative re-structuring.
-Central Bank governor Salameh heads to Cambodia today to take part in the third meeting for the central banks governors of the Francophone countries.

-Interior Minister Murr expects to uncover within 48 hours events surrouding the killing by police on Sunday of a Palestinian accused of belonging to a gang charged with selling forged and genuine finance ministry revenue stamps.
